# Author notes (from the project owner)

**Rule for Claude sessions: do NOT edit this file unless the author explicitly tells you to.** Read it before every build or planning decision. It was written once by Claude on 2026-11-20 from the author's own answers in chat; the wording below is the author's intent.

## Goal
- Public benefit above all; utilitarian view: research whatever helps humanity most. Specific topics follow from feasibility.
- Real-world benefit is the main objective. Skills or portfolio are not the objective.
- Results are meant to give knowledge to people who can act on it (researchers, charities, policymakers). The author does not intend to publish under their own name.
- If a topic or method conflicts with public benefit (e.g. dual-use risk), do not do it. If there is no conflict, it is fine.

## Role of the author
- Decides: which topics get researched, and how much money is spent. Wants to be involved at nothing more than that, plus reports.
- The AI system should choose and propose problems itself (importance, tractability, neglectedness) and work with the author to pick the best ones.

## Constraints
- Budget: about 50 EUR/month possible (more if funding is found), on top of an existing 20 EUR/month Claude subscription.
- No server today, but the author is willing to set one up if it is the better way.
- No GPU.
- Author is a Mathematics BSc student (TU Dresden); not an expert in the research domains the system may touch.

## Decisions so far
- Do not write a new research framework from scratch if existing ones fit (see `framework-evaluation.md`).
